```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import HTML
from twinfault_site import *

p = sql("select * from fct_daily_pipeline order by date")
first, last = p.date.min(), p.date.max()
expected_days = (last - first).days + 1
gaps = int(p.missing_blocks.sum() + p.duplicate_blocks.sum())
usual_lag = p.max_load_lag_hours.median()
flags = sql("select * from pipeline_flags")
rules = impossible_summary()
src = source_status()
src_events = source_events()
late_arrivals = source_events(kinds=("arrived",))
late_days = int((flags.pipeline == "Late or rewritten").sum())
tests = dbt_test_count()
```

```{python}
#| title: Blocks per day (one block every 12 seconds would be 7,200)
fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_scatter(x=p.date, y=p.blocks, mode="lines", name="blocks", showlegend=False,
                line=dict(color="#2f6fd6", width=1.5), hovertemplate="%{y:,} blocks")
fig.add_hline(y=7200, line=dict(color=MUTED, dash="dot", width=1))
bad = p[(p.missing_blocks > 0) | (p.duplicate_blocks > 0)]
fig.add_scatter(x=bad.date, y=bad.blocks, mode="markers", name="gap or duplicate", showlegend=not bad.empty,
                marker=dict(color="#d1495b", size=9, symbol="x"), hovertemplate="%{x}: check this day<extra></extra>")
fig.update_yaxes(tickformat=",")
show(fig)
```

```{python}
#| title: Load delay per day (hours from block to file, slowest row, log scale)
fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_scatter(x=p.date, y=p.max_load_lag_hours, mode="lines", name="slowest row", showlegend=False,
                line=dict(color="#7b61c2", width=1.5), hovertemplate="%{y:.1f} h")
fig.add_scatter(x=[first, last], y=[2 * usual_lag] * 2, mode="lines", name="late or rewritten (twice the usual)",
                line=dict(color="#d1495b", dash="dot", width=1), hoverinfo="skip")
fig.update_yaxes(type="log", tickvals=[1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200, 300, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000])
show(fig)
```

## Row

```{python}
#| title: Days to check before explaining any move
issues = sql("""
    with t as (select date, sum(transfers) as transfers from fct_daily_payments group by date)
    select f.date, f.pipeline, p.missing_blocks, p.duplicate_blocks, p.max_load_lag_hours, t.transfers
    from pipeline_flags as f
    join fct_daily_pipeline as p using (date)
    left join t using (date)
    where f.pipeline <> 'OK'
    order by f.pipeline = 'Late or rewritten', p.max_load_lag_hours desc
""")
shown = issues.head(15)
if issues.empty:
    out = HTML('<p>No day has missing blocks, duplicate blocks or late or rewritten data, so no '
               'unusual day on this site can be put down to these pipeline checks.</p>')
else:
    table = pd.DataFrame({
        "Day": shown.date.dt.strftime("%a %d %b %Y"),
        "Verdict": shown.pipeline.map(pill),
        "Missing / duplicate blocks": [f"{m:,} / {d:,}" for m, d in zip(shown.missing_blocks, shown.duplicate_blocks)],
        "Slowest row": shown.max_load_lag_hours.map("{:,.0f} h".format),
        "Transfers": shown.transfers.map(compact),
    })
    more = (f'<p class="note">{len(issues):,} days in total; the {len(shown)} shown are '
            'block problems first, then the longest delays.</p>') if len(issues) > len(shown) else ""
    out = HTML(html_table(table, numeric=("Missing / duplicate blocks", "Slowest row", "Transfers")) + more)
out
```

```{python}
#| title: What is checked, and where
HTML(f"""
<ol>
<li><b>Extract</b> (monthly, from AWS): seven checks on every month, including continuous block
numbers, no duplicate blocks, and transfers with no missing amount or address.</li>
<li><b>dbt</b> (monthly): {tests or "the"} tests per month, including unique keys, accepted values,
no block gaps and a reconciliation that the daily cube adds up to the raw transfers exactly.
A month that fails is not uploaded.</li>
<li><b>Freshness</b>: the load log for last month must be less than 35 days old (warning)
or 62 days old (error).</li>
<li><b>Every row</b> (once, over the whole dataset): 16 rules that Ethereum itself makes
impossible to break, such as a transfer inside a failed transaction or a block whose parent is
not the block before it. Any hit would be a bug in the source. Results are in the table below.</li>
<li><b>The source itself</b> (every day): the last 14 days of the AWS source are measured every
morning, and every published day again every Sunday, the same way the load log measured them.
A day that arrives late, changes, or no longer matches what was loaded opens an issue on GitHub.
Results are at the bottom of this page.</li>
<li><b>This page</b>: a day is <i>late or rewritten</i> if its slowest row was written more than
twice the usual delay ({usual_lag:.0f} hours) after its block. Either the data arrived late, or the
source rewrote that day afterwards; both mean the day's numbers may have changed after they were
first published. What these days look like is shown on the
<a href="investigations.html#rewrites">Investigations</a> page.</li>
</ol>
<p class="note">The source data is AWS Public Blockchain Data, which AWS labels experimental.
That is why completeness is checked from the data itself: block numbers are sequential,
so a gap is visible without trusting the loader.</p>
""")
```

## Row {height=790px}

```{python}
#| title: Rules that cannot be broken on Ethereum, checked on every row
if rules.empty:
    out = HTML('<p>The every-row check has not been run yet.</p>')
else:
    total = int(rules.violations.sum())
    table = pd.DataFrame({
        "Rule": rules.check,
        "Table": rules.tbl,
        "A hit would mean a bug in": rules.fault.map({"source": "the source", "our extract": "our extract"}),
        "Rows checked": rules.rows_checked.map(lambda n: f"{int(n):,}"),
        "Rows breaking it": rules.violations.map(lambda n: f"{int(n):,}"),
        "Result": [pill("OK") if n == 0 else '<span class="pill pill-bad">Broken</span>' for n in rules.violations],
    })
    rows = int(rules.groupby("tbl").rows_checked.max().sum())
    headline = (f"<p><b>No row breaks any rule:</b> {rows:,} rows checked across all three tables.</p>" if total == 0
                else f"<p><b>{total:,} rows break a rule.</b> Each one is a bug in the source data.</p>")
    out = HTML(headline + html_table(table, numeric=("Rows checked", "Rows breaking it"))
               + '<p class="note">The checks already run before each upload (block gaps, duplicates, '
                 'missing values) are not repeated here.</p>')
out
```

## Row {height=400px}

```{python}
#| title: Has the AWS source changed since it was loaded?
def duration(hours: float) -> str:
    return f"{hours * 60:.0f} minutes" if hours < 1 else f"{hours:.1f} hours"

def days(n: int) -> str:
    return f"{n:,} day" if n == 1 else f"{n:,} days"

if src is None:
    out = HTML("<p>No snapshot summary yet. It appears after the next run of "
               "<i>Phase 6 - snapshot the source every day</i>.</p>")
else:
    parts = []
    whole = src["compared_table_days"] == src["published_table_days"]
    scope = (f"All {src['published_days']:,} published days ({src['compared_table_days']:,} table-days)" if whole
             else f"{src['compared_table_days']:,} of {src['published_table_days']:,} published table-days")
    when = pd.Timestamp(src["rechecked_by"]).strftime("%d %b %Y")
    if src["republished_table_days"] == 0:
        parts.append(f"<p><b>No published day has changed.</b> {scope} were measured again in the AWS "
                     f"source on {when} or later, and each matches what was loaded: rows, files, block "
                     "range and write times.</p>")
    else:
        n = src["republished_days"]
        parts.append(f"<p><b>{n:,} published {'day has' if n == 1 else 'days have'} changed since "
                     f"{'it was' if n == 1 else 'they were'} loaded</b> ({src['republished_table_days']:,} table-days, listed below). {scope} were "
                     f"measured again on {when} or later. Any number on this site for those days may differ "
                     "from the source today.</p>")
    late = late_arrivals[late_arrivals.hours_after_day > 48]
    late_dates = set(late.date)
    flagged = set(flags[flags.pipeline == "Late or rewritten"].date)
    if not late_dates:
        late_text = "No day was first written more than 48 hours after it ended."
    else:
        among = (f"{'it is' if len(late_dates) == 1 else f'all {len(late_dates):,} are'} among the "
                 f"{late_days:,} late or rewritten days above"
                 if late_dates <= flagged else
                 f"{len(late_dates & flagged):,} of them are among the {late_days:,} late or rewritten days above")
        late_text = (f"{days(len(late_dates))} {'was' if len(late_dates) == 1 else 'were'} first written more "
                     f"than 48 hours after {'it' if len(late_dates) == 1 else 'they'} ended: {among}.")
    parts.append(f"<p>Snapshots started on {pd.Timestamp(src['first_taken']):%d %b %Y}; the latest was taken "
                 f"{pd.Timestamp(src['last_taken']):%d %b %Y %H:%M} UTC. A day usually reaches the source "
                 f"{duration(src['median_arrival_hours'])} after it ends. {late_text}</p>")
    if src_events.empty:
        parts.append("<p>Since the snapshots started, no day has arrived late, changed, or stopped matching "
                     "what was loaded.</p>")
    else:
        kinds = {"late": ("Late", "warn"), "changed": ("Changed", "warn"), "republished": ("Differs from load", "bad")}
        shown = src_events.head(20)
        table = pd.DataFrame({
            "Seen": shown.seen_at.dt.strftime("%d %b %Y"),
            "Event": [f'<span class="pill pill-{kinds[k][1]}">{kinds[k][0]}</span>' for k in shown.kind],
            "Table": shown.source_table,
            "Day": shown.date.dt.strftime("%a %d %b %Y"),
            "What changed": [f'<span style="display:inline-block;white-space:normal;min-width:16rem">{d}</span>'
                             for d in shown.detail],
        })
        if len(src_events) > len(shown):
            parts.append(f'<p class="note">{len(src_events):,} events in total; {len(shown)} are shown, '
                         'differences from the load first, then changes, then days not yet in the source.</p>')
        parts.append(html_table(table))
    out = HTML("".join(parts))
out
```
